title: Twelve Columns and One Wrong Figure
subtitle: 数据与统计 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 数据与统计（科学与技术·数据与统计）
meta: 主题语境：数据与统计（科学与技术·数据与统计）　|　核心词汇：difference　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 difference 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1953 the statistician ① found a difference that no auditor in the office would have accepted, and she said the finding was the whole of the audit. The ② difference, meaning the gap and not the disagreement, ran twelve columns and stayed unexplained in the margin; a difference, she said, is the only thing in a table that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ difference in that table had the same wrong figure beside it, and the ④ difference at the end, meaning the one they kept for the annual return and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever checked twice. A difference, her assistant said, is nine parts checking and one part somebody willing to find; the statistician said the checking is the part that fills twelve columns.

The clerk meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the difference was the whole of the meeting, meaning the disagreement and not the gap. The ⑥ difference, meaning the disagreement and not any of that, is the only thing in a meeting that everybody mentions and nobody settles; difference, he said, is either something you find or the only word that means both a gap and a disagreement. He said the disagreement is the part they remember.

By 1961 the ⑦ difference had become a line in a report, and the report had become an argument about the wrong figure. The ⑧ difference of the whole thing, the statistician wrote in June, was one table and twelve columns of checking; difference, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to check. She said the checking was never mentioned.

The ⑨ difference I remember is the one at the end, which was settled in 1974 and is still described as the strangest in the office. A ⑩ difference, the assistant said in 1976, is the only thing that improves by being explained; every difference, she said, is a disagreement that has agreed to look like a gap. She said the disagreement was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 差别；差额（指表格里出现的那一处）
B. n. 差额（指那个差距本身，与那场分歧相对）
C. 固定搭配：find a difference 发现一处差额
D. n. 差额（指留给年度报表用的那一处）
E. n. 差异；差额（抽象总称，指一张表的全部出入）
F. n. 差额（指报告上写到、被列明的那一处）
G. n. 分歧；争论（指会议上出现的那一场）
H. n. 分歧（抽象总称，指人人提到却无人化解的那场）

items.q: found a difference that no auditor in the office would have accepted
The difference, meaning the gap and not the disagreement
the difference was the whole of the meeting
the difference had become a line in a report
The difference of the whole thing
A difference, the assistant said in 1976

answers.why: find a difference 意为“发现一处差额”，1953 年统计员发现了一处办公室里没有一位审计员肯接受的差额。
difference 意为“差额”，指那个差距本身而不是那场分歧，它横跨十二列而在页边没有说明。
difference 意为“差别、差额”，指那张表格里每一处差额，每一处旁边都有同一个错误的数字。
difference 意为“差额”，指留给年度报表用的那一处，是唯一有人核对过两次的。
difference 意为“分歧、争论”，指会议上出现的那一场，办事员说这场分歧就是那次会议的全部。
difference 意为“分歧”，指人人提到却无人化解的那场而不是那个差距，是会议里人人都提到、却无人化解的东西。
difference 意为“差额”，指报告上写到、被列明的那一处，到 1961 年这处差额成了报告里的一行。
difference 意为“差异、差额”，统计员六月写道，整件事的出入是一张表和十二列的核对。
difference 意为“分歧”，我记得的是末尾那一处，1974 年被化解，至今仍被说成办公室里最奇的一处。
difference 为抽象总称，助手 1976 年说，一处差额是唯一会因为被解释而变得更好的东西。
